summary: Closed-end cap (new pommel end) for a toy sword whose hollow two-shell plastic handle is broken open at the pommel end. The cap slides 15 mm over the broken end and is glued on. Per the user, the bore is straight and sized to the largest handle readings (31.6 wide x 28.3 thick) plus a 0.3 mm glue gap per side; glue fills the gap where the handle is thinner. Outside: a pommel-like outward bulge (2 mm per side at mid-height, circular arc) with three stepped chevron grooves on each wide face, echoing the handle's chevrons. 2.4 mm closed end with a 3 mm vent. PLA, closed end on the bed, open rim up, no supports.

assumptions: A1: straight bore at the largest readings (user: 'keep it thickest only'). The handle is thinner at the broken edge (19.9 thick there), so the gap there is up to about 4.5 mm per side on the narrow faces; the glue fills it. Use a gap-filling glue (2-part epoxy or hot glue), not thin superglue.
A2: the rounded-rectangle section (corner R8) approximates the handle's barrel section; the glue gap absorbs the difference.
A3: the cap only covers 15 mm of handle; it does not restore any length lost at the break.
A5: bed 250 x 210 (Prusa MK4 class), the same as the other projects; every Bambu bed is larger.
A6: the second sword in input/tapper/ is a reference only; its readings are not used for the bore.
A7: the outside is decorative: a 2 mm outward bulge (user) and stepped chevron grooves echoing the handle; the closed-end chamfer (former D15) is dropped because the bulge already rounds the base.
